axisNotes.brief: His support for a civic free press and electoral choice favours accountable institutions. Editorial control of his newspaper is reviewed separately from government electoral rights.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The 2024 endorsement reversal and 2025 restriction of opinion priorities weaken a simple press-pluralism account; neither establishes support for cancelling elections. Recall and binding referendums remain mixed representative-versus-direct-democracy estimates.

axisNotes.brief: His explicit personal-liberty commitment favours expression and private choices. For crime prevention, warrants and credible threats supply narrower grounds for intervention.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A newspaper owner’s editorial choices are not a state censorship policy. Personal drug use, random policing and firearms are extensions of his stated principle, not documented answers.

axisNotes.brief: Opposition to nationality-based entry restrictions and support for migrant inclusion favour cultural pluralism. Common language and participation can coexist with retained identities.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Immigration advocacy does not establish every cultural accommodation. Distinct identities taking unconditional priority and exemptions from general face-covering rules are separately conditional.

axisNotes.brief: His reported advocacy for migrants and Dreamers supports easier legal settlement and protection, not admission exclusively by skill.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Dreamer protection is narrower than unconditional permission for everyone who entered illegally to remain. Housing limits, benefit eligibility and nationality-based cultural preferences lack precise personal programmes.

axisNotes.brief: Defence contracting shows acceptance of military capability; his discussion of destructive AI and nuclear risk also supplies grounds for restraint.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Commercial defence support does not establish endorsement of an offensive war or autonomous lethal targeting. Diplomacy is preferred where compatible with defence; absolute avoidance of defending allies is unlikely.

axisNotes.brief: International scientific cooperation and space development favour collaboration while US contracts operate within national institutions.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Cross-border business is not endorsement of supranational courts or a world federation. Estimates preserve national exit, currency and border authority alongside shared practical programmes.

axisNotes.brief: His business model and market commitment favour private ownership, including regulated contractors. Public infrastructure spending remains compatible with private providers.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Tax-supported infrastructure does not imply nationalising healthcare, banks or housing. Mixed cases retain public access responsibilities without inventing a comprehensive privatisation manifesto.

axisNotes.brief: The market commitment and global commercial model support reduced trade barriers and consumer choice.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Strategic-security procurement and foreign control are conditional exceptions. No precise personal agricultural or retaliation policy was established.

axisNotes.brief: Market allocation receives strong support, while his infrastructure-tax endorsement admits targeted public investment.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Government contracts are not compulsory production targets. The minimum-wage item is assessed as a plausible floor, not a general government wage schedule; subsidy and investment-target questions remain conditional.

axisNotes.brief: The evidence combines limited-tax preferences with willingness to pay for public infrastructure. It does not make his private philanthropy equivalent to compulsory cash redistribution.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The corporate-tax concession prevents assigning blanket tax opposition. It does not settle inheritance, land redistribution or the size of cash transfers; these are lower-confidence item-specific estimates.

axisNotes.brief: A civic personal-liberty framework supports civil government independent of religious authority.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: An interfaith university ceremony is not evidence for official worship by government. Symbols, festivals and charity-related exemptions can receive a conditional answer without inferring theocracy from private belief.

axisNotes.brief: Personal choice and his rejection of idealising past living conditions support openness to social change.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Personal relationships are not an abortion or school curriculum platform. Gender-language and inherited-custom items have competing autonomy and continuity considerations rather than automatic progressive responses.

axisNotes.brief: His interviews favour development and AI opportunity, while distinguishing irreversible decisions and preservation of Earth.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Biomedical deployment requires a different risk threshold from productivity software. Brain implants, embryo enhancement and ecosystem safety are inferred separately; concern about irreversible harm is not erased by enthusiasm for space.

axisNotes.brief: His emphasis on reversible decisions and decentralised initiative makes regional discretion plausible, while nationwide infrastructure warrants coordination.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Corporate team autonomy is only a weak analogy to constitutional federalism. Emergency coordination is treated separately from ordinary local power; secession and indigenous institutions are mixed estimates.

axisNotes.brief: His account distinguishes cognitive gifts from learned kindness and describes formative family experiences. This supports a mixed causal account rather than universal genetic or environmental primacy.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Individual ability is not evidence for hereditary national IQ or racial violence. Temperament can have biological components while moral habits and cooperation remain largely learned; the exact empirical comparisons are not his published positions.

axisNotes.brief: His election campaigning and support for political alternatives favour electoral selection; his efficiency agenda creates tension over executive constraints.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Funding parties is not proof of equal competition. Judicial checks and executive override are mixed estimates given friction between democratic accountability and rapid executive action; military coups and indefinite postponement remain disfavoured.

axisNotes.brief: Free expression and voluntary personal choice have substantial weight, while order and prevention of violence retain roles.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The 2023 interview is not a full criminal-law programme. Allowing speech does not automatically establish protection for road-blocking demonstrations or disclosure of every classified document.

axisNotes.brief: Support for legal workers coexists with emphasis on integration and national cohesion in his contemporary political alignment.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Party endorsement does not transfer a whole party platform. His own migration history is not used as evidence of pluralism; language, ceremonies and religious clothing remain distinct weak inferences.

axisNotes.brief: The evidence favours lawful employment mobility, especially skilled recruitment, alongside enforcement against unlawful entry.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Support for H-1B visas and European workers is not open borders or skill-exclusive permanent residence. Family reunion is retained; automatic removal of every cap and refugee eligibility remain conditional.

axisNotes.brief: He advocates de-escalation of potentially catastrophic wars while supporting US military technology and capabilities.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The 2026 Pentagon advisory role qualifies any simple pacifist reading. His earlier opposition to escalation remains relevant; no evidence establishes blanket permission for machines to approve lethal attacks.

axisNotes.brief: National decision authority is compatible with negotiated trade and practical cross-border cooperation in his public activity.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Transatlantic free movement is not political federation. Defence advice to the US is not evidence against every alliance; currency, courts and border-sharing are evaluated separately.

axisNotes.brief: Entrepreneurial provision and private competition are favoured over broad nationalisation.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Commercial space contracts do not prove that all public services should be sold. Security can be protected by regulation of private firms; a strategic exception remains possible.

axisNotes.brief: His explicit zero-tariff proposal favours freer trade even while he works with protectionist political allies.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The proposal concerns Europe and North America, not an unconditional manifesto for all products. Security-related foreign ownership and subsidy disputes remain mixed; answers are not copied from Trump.

axisNotes.brief: Market decisions and deregulation are favoured, with technology programmes sometimes benefiting from targeted state demand.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Government contracting does not by itself establish support for compulsory production plans. Subsidies and health or safety floors can differ from centrally assigned wages and prices.

axisNotes.brief: Public-spending reduction and tax restraint receive weight, alongside the possibility of income support during technological disruption.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Opposition to spending does not mean opposition to every safety net. Cash floors and low-paid-worker supplements remain mixed; private wealth alone is not the evidence for these choices.

axisNotes.brief: Civil liberties suggest independent civil law, with room for cultural recognition of religious holidays.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Private spirituality and political alliances do not establish clerical government. State-foundation and symbol questions remain conditional; faith cultivation in public schools is less likely.

axisNotes.brief: His contemporary political interventions favour some traditional family and sex-role expectations while retaining individual choice in other areas.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A Republican endorsement is not agreement with every abortion or marriage plank. Same-sex recognition and gender-language conventions are separately assessed; personal family structure is not substituted for a social doctrine.

axisNotes.brief: He favours ambitious technologies and augmentation while raising concerns about AI and civilization-scale risk.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A brain-device company does not imply support for human embryo enhancement. Therapeutic implants, healthy enhancement, diagnostic reliability and irreversible harms have different safeguards.

axisNotes.brief: Deregulation and competition across jurisdictions favour regional freedom, while national economic and security projects favour coordination.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: DOGE involvement is federal action, not a complete federalism doctrine. Regional constitutions and tax autonomy can coexist with national disaster response; secession and indigenous powers lack precise commitments.

axisNotes.brief: His neurological technology work supplies a biological component; his accounts of social conflict also give learning and incentives substantial causal weight.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Neural circuitry does not establish inherited racial differences. Gender and temperament estimates are qualified; racial IQ and violence claims are not attributed to him from technological interest.

axisNotes.brief: His participation in electoral initiatives and campaigning supports representative government with civic accountability, rather than selection by a business elite.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Expertise in public health is not a proposal to replace voters. Recall and binding repeal votes balance democratic participation with stable representative processes.

axisNotes.brief: His emphasis on responsible public institutions supports safeguards and lawful intervention while retaining civil expression and due process.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Pandemic protection against transmission differs from coercion aimed only at an adult’s own wellbeing. Preventive policing powers are more conditional than criticism or warrants.

axisNotes.brief: His stated need for varied global backgrounds and work across communities favour cultural inclusion and accommodation.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Global health work does not establish cultural identities overriding shared civic responsibilities. Language and calendar arrangements remain mixed practical estimates.

axisNotes.brief: His international work and support for opportunity make legal mobility and protection more likely than skill-only settlement.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Funding health overseas is not an admission policy. Numerical ceilings, undocumented regularisation and welfare eligibility are educated extensions, not claimed personal legislation.

axisNotes.brief: Cooperation and preserving human lives favour diplomacy, with legitimate defensive force still possible.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Global-health activity is weaker evidence on military posture than on aid. Absolute refusal to defend an ally is not inferred; conscription and autonomous lethal targeting are distinct lower-confidence estimates.

axisNotes.brief: His pooled global-health approach and call for AI institutions favour shared international programmes and some binding standards.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A multilateral nonprofit is not a world government. Domestic courts, currency, borders and treaty exit have conditional answers rather than automatic transfer of all sovereignty.

axisNotes.brief: He distinguishes the useful roles of government, private enterprise and foundations. Public education and health commitments coexist with competitive commercial providers.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Public financing does not imply that every school, hospital or insurer must be publicly owned. The mixed ownership items preserve that distinction and are not used to manufacture a moderate score.

axisNotes.brief: International exchange and global scientific cooperation favour trade openness with practical safeguards.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: US-China dialogue is not an unconditional agricultural or national-security policy. Retaliation, subsidised imports and strategic control remain conditional cases.

axisNotes.brief: Market incentives coexist with public investment, coordination and new institutions addressing market failures.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The 2026 AI risk assessment increases support for regulation and coordination, but does not establish compulsory production quotas or routine nationwide allocation of all goods.

axisNotes.brief: He explicitly supports progressive taxation of capital and estates, stronger government revenue and public services while preserving incentives.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Tax proposals are not a promise to equalise all incomes. Wealth transfers, work requirements and land redistribution remain inferences; philanthropy is not substituted for tax support.

axisNotes.brief: Civil institutions and universal public-service obligations favour secular legal authority.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Personal faith would not establish a state religion. Ceremonial recognition, public symbols and charitable exemptions remain mixed rather than being automatically rejected.

axisNotes.brief: His criticism of early exclusion of women and emphasis on broader opportunity favour changing restrictive social conventions.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: This is not a detailed abortion, sex-education or adoption manifesto. Recognition of diverse families does not require rejecting every inherited custom or gradual reform.

axisNotes.brief: He supports technology for health and climate, but contemporary AI concerns favour precaution and accountable institutions in high-risk uses.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: His current caution about AI is preserved rather than extrapolating 2019 optimism unchanged. Productivity adoption, diagnostic safeguards, biological enhancement and general irreversibility are separate decisions.

axisNotes.brief: He backs local and state initiatives while calling for coordinated national and international responses to large public-health and AI problems.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Supporting a Washington state income tax is direct context for regional fiscal discretion, not proof of a secession position. National standards can coexist with local delivery and land management.

axisNotes.brief: His emphasis on education, opportunity and childhood conditions supports social explanations, with individual neurodevelopment also recognised.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Recognition of autism or temperament is not a racial heredity claim. Attention, stress and attraction remain mixed biological-social cases; precise comparative causation is low-confidence.

axisNotes.brief: His public speech places political expression within democratic participation; electoral choice and rights checks are the most likely governing principles.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: His own company’s concentrated voting control is not government autocracy. Moderation changes and rapprochement with an incumbent do not establish opposition-party bans.

axisNotes.brief: The recent shift gives speech and reduced censorship more weight, with criminal threats and court-supervised investigation still distinguished.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Corporate moderation and state law are different. Real-name platform practice does not prove support for state identification; classified disclosure and firearms remain mixed estimates.

axisNotes.brief: The inclusion and opportunity letter favours plural identities; reduced moderation does not itself endorse intolerance or require abandoning that earlier position.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Accommodation spending and cultural calendars are not established by a platform’s speech policy. Shared civic participation can coexist with retaining cultural identity.

axisNotes.brief: His backed reform combines legalisation, family and skilled entry with border enforcement, rather than unconditional open borders.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The bipartisan reform’s conditions prevent interpreting regularisation as no enforcement. The 2025 moderation change is not evidence that his immigration programme became restrictive.

axisNotes.brief: Defence collaboration supports capability and US security interests, while his civic speech does not establish enthusiasm for intervention.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Military augmented reality is not autonomous permission to kill. Maintaining forces and preferring diplomacy can coexist; pre-emptive and coercive-force hypotheticals are qualified estimates.

axisNotes.brief: Recent resistance to foreign constraints on American platforms gives national authority weight, while global connection and cooperation remain supported.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A global user base does not imply supranational courts. National corporate interests do not prove opposition to all treaties; foreign-policy blocs and common standards are separately assessed.

axisNotes.brief: Private innovation is central to his work, with public access and education receiving support through partnerships.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Charitable education support does not settle ownership of schools or hospitals. Broad privatisation is inferred cautiously, with mixed housing and broadcaster questions.

axisNotes.brief: He favours cross-border access and objects to foreign restrictions on US online providers.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Defending American firms can support a security exception without establishing tariffs on every product. Strategic acquisitions and subsidised imports differ from consumer service access.

axisNotes.brief: Private enterprise and product development support market allocation, with some room for public investment and basic safeguards.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: CZI’s equality goals are not a central production plan. Minimum wages, public subsidies and directed bank lending remain separate estimates, not assumed from Meta’s business model alone.

axisNotes.brief: The opportunity letter supports improving low-income lives through institutions and philanthropy, but does not endorse a complete compulsory transfer programme.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Private giving is not proof of wealth-tax support. A basic floor and earned-income supplements can coexist with market incentives; income compression and estate taxation remain mixed.

axisNotes.brief: Protection of varied religious expression and civil rights supports secular legal institutions.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: His personal faith is not used to assign official religious law. Ceremonies, symbols and religious charities have mixed civic-versus-cultural implications.

axisNotes.brief: Earlier inclusion of sexual orientation and gender identity coexists with a later rejection of some speech restrictions.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Allowing contentious opinions is not personal opposition to same-sex families. Language prescriptions, family teaching and gradual institutional reform remain conditional.

axisNotes.brief: His current AI statement opposes coordinated slowdown and favours putting technology into users’ hands, alongside biomedical ambition.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Brain augmentation and embryo enhancement are not settled by wearables or disease research. Patient reliability and irreversible harm retain higher safety thresholds than consumer software.

axisNotes.brief: Local community partnerships support discretion, while nationwide rules and American defence policy support coordination where scale matters.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Corporate decentralisation is not proof of constitutional secession. Regional tax authority and local service delivery are plausible; disaster response warrants national coordination.

axisNotes.brief: The letter explicitly links early nutrition, trauma and social exclusion to development and opportunity, favouring environmental explanations for many behaviours.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The account is not a denial of genetic temperament or an empirical position on attractiveness. Those questions remain mixed; racial determinism is not inferred from political or speech changes.

axisNotes.brief: His critique of democracy’s compatibility with freedom reduces confidence in majoritarian mechanisms; his clarification rejects disenfranchising any class.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: The essay is not a proposal for military rule or election cancellation. Electoral campaigning supplies counter-evidence; expert selection and unconstrained executive control remain mixed rather than falsely documented autocratic commitments.

axisNotes.brief: Voluntary personal choice and opposition to coercion coexist with investment in security technology.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Security investments do not establish endorsement of indefinite detention or every surveillance tool. Court authorisation is separated from suspicionless multi-year movement records.

axisNotes.brief: His national political rhetoric gives shared civic identity priority while allowing individual identity.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Gay identity is not evidence of a multicultural policy. A national political coalition is weaker evidence on signage, holidays and dress-law exemptions; those remain conditional.

axisNotes.brief: His national renewal arguments make controlled immigration plausible while retaining useful legal employment and family routes.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: National identity does not establish skill-exclusive settlement or a ban on refugees. Precise asylum quotas, cultural selection and permanent-residence sponsorship remain low-confidence extensions.

axisNotes.brief: He opposes unsuccessful interventionist wars while supporting defence capability and security investment.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Opposition to Iraq and Libya is not absolute pacifism. Palantir investment is not direct approval of unsupervised lethal targeting; capability and diplomatic concessions are separately assessed.

axisNotes.brief: His objections to global political consolidation favour national sovereignty and political exit.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Practical cooperation remains possible without a world state. Common trade rules and pooled health or environmental spending are conditional, not treated as equivalent to federation.

axisNotes.brief: Private enterprise and alternatives to state monopoly favour private ownership and contracting.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: His recognition of past government research allows public investment without nationalising firms. Strategic ownership is a mixed security case rather than automatically private.

axisNotes.brief: The Press Club speech challenges the claim that all trade outcomes benefit everyone; entrepreneurial freedom still favours exchange.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: This tension prevents copying a blanket free-trade or protectionist pattern. Domestic capability and strategic foreign control get greater caution than online services or ordinary sourcing.

axisNotes.brief: His stated opposition to collectivist direction favours market prices and entrepreneurial entry, with exceptional state research compatible with that outlook.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Criticism of trade outcomes is not a national production plan. Private-currency competition is grounded in his essay’s account of PayPal; subsidies and strategic investment remain conditional.

axisNotes.brief: His opposition to confiscatory taxation and welfare-state constraints supports limited compulsory redistribution and retaining earnings.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: A limited safety net is distinguished from abolition of all aid. Land transfers and detailed working-age conditions remain inferred, not positions proved by his wealth.

axisNotes.brief: Religious ideas influence his public political analysis, while his liberty argument opposes compulsory collective authority.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Christian belief and apocalyptic rhetoric do not establish clerical vetoes or religious courts. Cultural religious recognition is more plausible than compulsory faith instruction or replacing civil law.

axisNotes.brief: His opposition to cultural conformity coexists with national-conservative commitments and explicit distance from parts of the Republican platform.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: His sexuality does not settle adoption or abortion policy. Same-sex recognition is estimated from stated individual identity and rejection of culture-war distraction, not from group identity alone.

axisNotes.brief: He favours technological escape from stagnation and mortality, while acknowledging catastrophic risks.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Technological progress is not unconditional embryo policy. Medical safety and irreversible civilization-scale risks receive separate qualified treatment; anti-global-government rhetoric does not erase risk concern.

axisNotes.brief: Seasteading and exit from political monopolies support decentralised jurisdictional choice; national defence can still require coordination.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Voluntary new jurisdictions differ from every contested secession claim. Indigenous local powers and healthcare coverage remain mixed; emergency coordination is assessed on scale, not ordinary centralisation.

axisNotes.brief: His endorsement of mimetic theory gives learned imitation, rivalry and social institutions significant causal weight, alongside individual talents.
axisNotes.counterEvidence: Contrarian politics is not genetic determinism. Mimetic desire does not answer national IQ or individual stress biology; learned conflict is distinguished from inherited racial violence.

accessLimitations: The New York Times June 2025 Thiel interview and its archive mirror were inaccessible; neither is cited as read. WIRED and the actual 2009 essay, 2016 Press Club transcript and 2011 mimetic-theory interview supply the retained context.
Some video sources returned their description and chapters rather than a full transcript. Those support broad interview context only, not verbatim unobserved statements.
The 2026 Gates Notes AI memo returned no readable body; the readable Axios interview was used instead.

The Washington Post Bezos report is not independent of its owner; it is cross-checked with AP, Princeton, Lex Fridman and Axios. CZI and Meta are not independent of Zuckerberg; FactCheck.org, AP and Le Monde provide contextual cross-checks.
Research checks were made for all five subjects through the stated cutoff. No claim is made that absence of a newer statement proves an older view unchanged.
